integrity: For every adjacent edge pair in a complete split graph, the exact local edge resolving neighborhood consists of the two nonshared endpoints. When the clique has at least two vertices, every unordered vertex pair can occur as such a nonshared-endpoint pair, forcing every generator to omit at most one vertex. For a star, only leaf pairs arise, so the center is unrestricted and at most one leaf may be omitted. The verifier reconstructs edge distances directly and checks all parameter pairs through six by six.
scientific_limitations: The one-edge graph K2 is separated because the defining convention requires a nonempty generator.
The theorem concerns local edge resolution only; ordinary edge, fractional, local vertex, and partition variants are outside scope.
The introducing paper already contains the scalar star case; the new result is the complete-split all-set classification and the second-clique-vertex transition.
Finite exhaustive verification for 1 <= m,n <= 6 is corroborative only.
A differently named or non-indexed complete-split treatment may exist despite targeted searches.
title: All local edge resolving sets of complete split graphs
